Q4 crude throughput is guided to 560k–600k bpd, reflecting the El Dorado turnaround.

writeup.headline: HF Sinclair rates Buy on a net-cash balance sheet, low absolute multiples and strong price trend.
writeup.thesis: HF Sinclair scores 70, a Buy, carried mainly by its balance sheet (94), trend (86) and valuation (80). The company holds net cash, with cash covering debt 1.2 times. In absolute terms the multiples are low: 0.6x sales, 5.9x free cash flow and 4.0x EV/EBIT, with an FCF yield 12.1 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield. Against its own history valuation sits near the middle of its own history (the multiples disagree: P/S expensive, P/FCF middle, EV/EBIT cheap). Growth (53) and quality (58) hold the score back: latest-quarter revenue growth of 49.7% year on year sits alongside a TTM revenue decline of 28.9%, and margins are thin, with an 18.0% gross margin and a 13.5% operating margin, typical of refining.
key_risks: Q3 adjusted EPS of $11.75 was partly flattered by a $600M SRE RIN benefit that may not recur.
Refining margins are cyclical; growth slowed by 3.4 pp from the previous quarter.
The El Dorado turnaround is expected to lower Q4 throughput, and capital spending guidance was raised.
Small refinery exemption litigation with the EPA is unresolved, and third-party challenges to the August 2026 grants are pending.
After shares rose 99.0% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago, the price is 44.0% above its 200-day average, leaving room for a pullback.
what_would_change: A drop of 6 points would move the rating to Hold, for example if refining margins fade and trend or news risk scores weaken.
A gain of 10 points would reach Strong Buy, which would likely need sustained revenue growth lifting the growth factor from 53.
Clearer, lasting margin and free cash flow improvement beyond one-off RIN benefits could raise the quality score from 58.
An adverse SRE ruling or a guidance cut would pressure the news risk score of 65.
